dct_description_sm: Over the years, the Tsilhqot'in people have been experiencing significant changes throughout the Territory. Although there are multiple drivers of change, many can be attributed to a warming climate. Historically, the region has experienced substantial warming. Some of the most significant changes witnessed by the Tsilhqot'in people include those brought by the mountain pine beetle epidemic, as well as the impact of warming water temperatures on their fish and fish habitat. The Tsilhqot'in culture, language and history is intrinsically linked to their environment and traditional lands. The changes and impacts of climate change poses a significant threat to the Tsilhqot'in way of life and the traditional practices, knowledge and beliefs of the people. The purpose of this project was to identify and document the changes experienced within the Territory over the last few decades, as well as the impacts of, and vulnerability to, climate change in the Territory. The ultimate goal of this project was to initiate a conversation on adaptation options to minimize any adverse impacts of climate change to Tsilhqot'in land, water, air and living systems, while protecting and improving the cultural resilience of the Tsilhqotin people for generations to come.
